last_message:
The docs now match the 5-attempt capture code. I changed two pages; nothing else in `docs/` mentioned the old count.

**`docs/features/payments.md`**
- **Retries:** now says a capture makes up to 5 attempts (`ATTEMPTS`), waiting 2, 4, 6 and then 8 seconds between them (`BACKOFF_SECONDS`). That means a member can wait up to 20 seconds longer on the confirmation page.
- **Why it changed:** I copied the reasons from the issue thread onto the page, because the docs are the source of truth and the notes may not stay. The gateway is slow every Friday from 17:00 to 19:00. The 3 old attempts went out within one second, so 58 orders were never charged and a volunteer had to charge them by hand. Replaying those timeouts with the new spacing, 57 of the 58 went through. Switching gateways was ruled out because the contract runs to December 2026.
- **Opening paragraph:** now mentions both reasons for the retry rules — the Friday slowdowns and the 2024 double charges.

**`docs/runbooks/gateway-timeouts.md`**
- The expected log output is now five `GatewayTimeout` lines per order that gave up, not three, with a link to the retry rules.

I didn't write a decision record. The repo's one record is about a basic design choice, and the sessions page handles a changed limit the same way I've done here: on the feature page.

Two things to check, since I had no one to ask:
- **Dates don't line up.** The issue's comments are dated Nov 15–24 with no year, but you said the change landed last week, and today is Oct 30. So I left out the year of the Friday incident.
- **Log lines aren't verified.** The runbook's "one line per attempt" assumes the worker logs every timeout. I couldn't confirm that in the code, because `capture.py` only raises the error after the last attempt. I only changed the count.

I didn't run the tests, since only docs changed.
